statement: The cue's +37-point gain at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 comes from robustness to sampling noise, not from choosing between two modes of fixed accuracy: the plain base's terse, non-deliberative answers are reasonably accurate (about 60 % at T 0.6) but at full temperature are derailed after their opening by sampled tail tokens, while the deliberative '\nOkay' register (cued or self-opened) checks itself and survives untruncated sampling; the opening selects robustness to noise, and later tokens decide whether the terse register fails.
why_strongest: It reproduces the three measured values. (1) D = 0: self-opened plain answers and cued answers are the same self-checking register, so they are equally robust at T 1.0 on the same problems. (2) R = 1.21: that register is long whichever way it is entered, and a little longer when entered without the cue. (3) AUROC 0.54: which register a sample enters is close to per-sample noise. It also explains board facts that the theory has to place outside its scope or list as conflicts. Going from T 0.6 to T 1.0 costs the plain base about 19 points (63.8 -> 44.8; 28-30 points on the short problems, 0 on the longest, knowledge-9e4147). The cue is worth only +7 to +12 points at T 0.6 (plain 319 vs cue 354-378, result-7968b8, result-e870a1, result-dadeec) but +37 at T 1.0. So the gain is mostly the terse register collapsing under full-temperature sampling, which fits published evidence that untruncated T 1.0 sampling hurts plain chain-of-thought (2407.01082: GSM8K 17.5 with temperature alone vs 27.7-30.9 with truncation). In the theory, the 'plain mode' has one low accuracy (about 0.26-0.30) as a property of the mode. In the rival, that accuracy is set by temperature, and the terse register is nearly as good as the cued one when sampling is cooler.

tests.experiment: Temperature sensitivity of the non-self-opened plain register: accuracy of non-self-opened plain base answers at T 0.6 minus accuracy of non-self-opened plain base answers at T 1.0, on the same problems.
tests.recipe: Files: S3 r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl; base, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) and S3 T3.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl; base, plain, T 1.0). In P_math500 keep, for each problem_index, only the row with the smallest value of the sample column. In T3 keep one row per problem_index. Score every kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. A row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay' (a newline immediately followed by 'Okay'), else non-self-opened. Let S = the problem_index values present in both files whose kept rows are non-self-opened in both files. A06 = mean v3 score of the P_math500 rows in S. A10 = mean v3 score of the T3 rows in S. Report A06 - A10. Problems missing from either file are dropped.
tests.theory_should_say: The theory treats the plain mode as one whole mode with its own low accuracy, so the non-self-opened answers should score about the same at both temperatures (a difference near 0 to +0.1). The rival puts the whole T 0.6 -> T 1.0 loss in this register and gives about +0.29.

tests.experiment: How weak the non-self-opened plain register is when sampling is cooler: accuracy of non-self-opened plain base answers at T 0.6 minus accuracy of cued base answers at T 0.6 on the same problems.
tests.recipe: Files: S3 r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (base, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) and S3 r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl; base, cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). In each file keep, for each problem_index, only the row with the smallest value of the sample column. Score every kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. A P_math500 row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay', else non-self-opened. Let S = the problem_index values whose kept P_math500 row is non-self-opened and which also have a kept F_math500 row. A = mean v3 score of the P_math500 rows in S. B = mean v3 score of the F_math500 rows in S. Report A - B. Problems missing from either file are dropped.
tests.theory_should_say: The cue's effect is a switch from a plain mode about 50 points weaker than the cued mode, so the non-self-opened plain answers should fall far below cued answers on the same problems: around -0.3 to -0.5, even after allowing for cued loops at T 0.6. The rival says the terse register is only about 10 points behind once sampling is cooler.

tests.experiment: Accuracy gap between self-opened and non-self-opened plain base answers at T 0.6, within one file.
tests.recipe: File: S3 r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (base, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). Keep, for each problem_index, only the row with the smallest value of the sample column. Score each kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. A row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay', else non-self-opened. Report (mean v3 score of the self-opened rows) - (mean v3 score of the non-self-opened rows). If either group is empty, report nothing.
tests.theory_should_say: The theory says the self-opened answers are a different whole mode, about 50 points better than the others (0.82 vs about 0.3 at T 1.0), so it should predict a large positive gap (about +0.3 to +0.5) here as well. The rival says that at T 0.6 the terse register is not derailed, so the gap shrinks to about +0.1.
